items.note: Used in shops etc. to welcome customers; literally means "Please come in."
Demonstrative pronoun — indicates something near the listener (see これ (kore)/あれ (are))

みせて (misete) is the て-form of みせる (miseru, 'to show'), so みせてください (misete kudasai) follows the same [て-form + ください] pattern as ちょっとまってください (chotto matte kudasai) from an earlier lesson; say [thing] を (o) みせてください to ask a shop to let you look closer at it.
Used mostly in いくらですか (ikura desu ka), 'how much is it?' — pair it with これ/それ/あれ (kore/sore/are) as the subject, e.g. これはいくらですか (kore wa ikura desu ka).
Suffix — attaches directly after a number (written 〜えん (en) in the source), e.g. 3,000えん (3,000en)
Demonstrative pronoun — indicates something distant from both speaker and listener (see これ (kore)/それ (sore))

items.note: Replaces は (wa) or が (ga) on the noun it marks (not added alongside them) to mean 'also/too'; contrast と (to), which just connects two nouns rather than adding meaning to one.

This じゃ (ja, 'well then') is a filler word marking a conclusion — not the same じゃ in じゃありません (ja arimasen) from an earlier lesson, which is a contraction of では (dewa) plus the negative; same sound, different job.
"noun を (o) ください (kudasai)" used when shopping or ordering; compare おねがいします (onegaishimasu), which can also be used to request an action or service

items.note: Uses the particle も (mo) (…either) in a negative sentence.
100 stands alone as ひゃく (hyaku), no いち (ichi, 'one') prefix needed, unlike 10,000, which requires いちまん (ichiman) rather than just まん (man).
300 changes ひゃく (hyaku) to びゃく (byaku) after さん (san), giving さんびゃく (sanbyaku) rather than さんひゃく (sanhyaku); the same kind of sound shift happens in 600 (ろっぴゃく, roppyaku) and 800 (はっぴゃく, happyaku).
10,000 needs the いち (ichi, 'one') prefix, いちまん (ichiman), unlike 100 or 1,000, which stand alone as ひゃく (hyaku) and せん (sen) without it.
8,000 doubles the consonant: はち (hachi) + せん (sen) becomes はっせん (hassen), not はちせん (hachisen). A similar shift happens in 3,000 (さんぜん, sanzen) and in hundreds like 600 (ろっぴゃく, roppyaku).
800 doubles the consonant and shifts ひゃく (hyaku) to ぴゃく (pyaku): はち (hachi) + ひゃく (hyaku) becomes はっぴゃく (happyaku). The same kind of shift happens in 300 (さんびゃく, sanbyaku) and 600 (ろっぴゃく, roppyaku).

600 doubles the consonant and shifts ひゃく (hyaku) to ぴゃく (pyaku): ろく (roku) + ひゃく (hyaku) becomes ろっぴゃく (roppyaku), not ろくひゃく (rokuhyaku). The same kind of shift happens in 300 (さんびゃく, sanbyaku) and 800 (はっぴゃく, happyaku).

せん (sen) shifts to ぜん (zen) after さん (san): さん (san) + せん (sen) becomes さんぜん (sanzen), a similar sound change to 8,000 (はっせん, hassen). Compare さんぜんえん (sanzen'en, '3,000 yen'), which adds the えん (en) counter.

items.note: てん (ten) marks the decimal point when reading a number aloud, so each digit after it is read individually, e.g. れいてんなな (rei ten nana), '0.7', rather than as a whole number.
Example of reading a decimal: れい (rei) (zero) + てん (ten) (point) + なな (nana) (seven)
ぶん (bun) marks the denominator in a fraction, spoken as [denominator]ぶんの (bun no) [numerator], e.g. にぶんのいち (nibun no ichi), '1/2'.
Example fraction reading: denominator + ぶんの (bun no) + numerator
Colloquial shortening of シャープペンシル (shāpupenshiru)
カード (kaado) here means a payment/credit card specifically — a business card is めいし (meishi) from an earlier lesson, not カード.
